    # =========================================================================
# web/views/inscription.py: “Create a Customer Account”: a patient who does not
# an account yet creates one themselves. Routes PUBLIQUES (we don’t have an account yet,
# by definition):
#
#    POST /registration/acc  ess "Create a Customer Account" button on the page
#                              authentication page: verifies the CAPTCHA from CETTE
#                              page, then opens the form
#    GE T /registrat        ion the form
#    POST /registrati        on creates the account, then returns to the login page
#
# The flow is protected against bots by the UN CAPTCHA on the
# authentication page:
#    1. The "Create a Customer Account" button sends the login form to
#       /registration/access; if the CAPTCHA is entered correctly, the server issues a
#       token (see security/passe_inscription.py);
#    2. Without a valid pass, /registration redirects to the
#       authentication page (decorator @passe_inscription_exige);
#    3. The token is consumed upon creation: a solved CAPTCHA allows
#       create a UN account;
#    4. Additionally, the number of accounts created per hour per IP address is limited
#       (see security/limiteur.py).
#
# The account created is exactly the one that ADMIN would create from the "Clients" page
# (same business-layer method: ajouter_client), except that the patient
# CHOISIT their username and password (required, with confirmation).
# =========================================================================

from urllib.parse import urlencode

from django.contrib import messages
from django.shortcuts import redirect, render
from django.urls import reverse
from django.utils.translation import gettext as _, ngettext
from django.views.decorators.http import require_http_methods, require_POST

from metier.erreurs import MetierErreur
from securite import captchas, limiteur, passe_inscription
from securite.passe_inscription import passe_inscription_exige

from .. import outils
from ..application import application
from ..formulaires import InscriptionForm
from .personnes import CHAMPS_ERREURS_METIER


# the message “too many accounts created,” in singular or plural form
def trop_de_comptes(minutes: int) -> str:
    return ngettext(
        "Trop de comptes ont été créés depuis votre connexion. Réessayez dans %(minutes)d minute.",
        "Trop de comptes ont été créés depuis votre connexion. Réessayez dans %(minutes)d minutes.",
        minutes) % {"minutes": minutes}


# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# POST /registration/login   fields: captcha_id, CAPTCHA (those on the
# authentication page; login and password, which are also sent, are ignored)
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
@require_POST
def acces(request):
    ip = outils.ip(request)
     # too many accounts created recently from this address: no need to proceed further
    minutes = limiteur.minutes_blocage_inscription(ip)
    if minutes > 0:
        messages.error(request, trop_de_comptes(minutes))
        return redirect("login")
     # captcha missing or incorrect: return to the authentication page, with a
     # new image (one failure counts as a failed login attempt)
    if not captchas.verifier(request.POST.get("captcha_id", ""), request.POST.get("captcha", "")):
        limiteur.echec_login(ip, "")
        messages.error(request, _("Pour créer un compte, recopiez d'abord correctement les "
                                  "caractères de l'image, puis cliquez sur « Créer un compte client »."))
        return redirect("login")
     # Correct CAPTCHA: Grant access and display the form
    return passe_inscription.emettre(redirect("inscription"))


# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# GET /registration: the form; POST /registration: creation. The
# The token has been verified AVANT the view is called (@passe_inscription_exige).
# The form validates TOUTE the input (fields and password confirmation):
# The user corrects all errors at once
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
@require_http_methods(["GET", "POST"])
@passe_inscription_exige
def inscription(request):
    if request.method == "GET":
        return page(request, InscriptionForm(initial={"titre": "Mr"}))
    formulaire = InscriptionForm(request.POST)
    if not formulaire.is_valid():
        return page(request, formulaire)
    ip = outils.ip(request)
     # 1. Have too many accounts been created recently from this address?
    minutes = limiteur.minutes_blocage_inscription(ip)
    if minutes > 0:
        return page(request, formulaire, trop_de_comptes(minutes))
     # 2. Account creation (customer + account USER, in a single transaction)
    donnees = formulaire.donnees()
    try:
        application().ajouter_client(donnees)
    except MetierErreur as e:
         # username or first name + last name already taken: the pass remains valid
        return page(request, formulaire, e.message, CHAMPS_ERREURS_METIER.get(e.code, []))
     # 3. The passcode has been used: it cannot be used to create a second account
    passe_inscription.consommer(request.COOKIES.get(passe_inscription.COOKIE))
    limiteur.inscription_reussie(ip)
     # 4. Return to the login page; username pre-filled
    messages.success(request, _("Votre compte a été créé. Vous pouvez vous connecter avec "
                                "le login %(login)s.") % {"login": donnees.login})
    url = f"{reverse('login')}?{urlencode({'login': donnees.login})}"
    return passe_inscription.effacer_cookie(redirect(url))


# The form; a rejected form: error code 422
def page(request, formulaire, erreur=None, champs_invalides=()):
    refuse = erreur is not None or (formulaire.is_bound and bool(formulaire.errors))
    return render(request, "inscription.html", {
        "titre_page": _("Créer un compte client"),
        "formulaire": formulaire.signaler(champs_invalides), "erreur": erreur,
    }, status=422 if refuse else 200)

    The patient creates a customer account themselves. The flow is protected by a CAPTCHA, the same one used on the login page.

    • Lines 59–75: The “Create a Customer Account” button on the login page submits the login form to this address (which later becomes the template [login.html]). If too many accounts have been created recently from this address (IP), there is no need to proceed further. If the CAPTCHA is missing or incorrect: return to the login page with a new image and a message; the failure counts as a failed login attempt (with an empty username). If the CAPTCHA is correct: a token is stored in a cookie, and the user is redirected to the form;
    • lines 84–91: the form. The [@passe_inscription_exige] decorator (line 85) checks the token before calling the view. The order of the decorators matters: the one closest to the function is applied first; [require_http_methods], placed above, therefore rejects a prohibited method before any other checks. The form validates the entire input, including password confirmation: the user sees all their errors at once;
    • Lines 92–111: account creation. The client and their account are created using the same business-logic method as for the administrator ([ajouter_client]); only the username and password are chosen by the patient. If a username or a homonym is already taken: return to the form without consuming the token. Creating an account consumes the token (one solved CAPTCHA equals one account), counts toward the hourly limit, and redirects to the login page with the username pre-filled (parameter [?login=...], generated by [urlencode]), along with a success message. The pass cookie is cleared.

    # =========================================================================
# web/views/espace.py: the patient’s pages (role USER), the one they
# sees immediately after logging in:
#
#    GE T /my-space               home page: [Gérer mon compte], [View a
#                                   calendar], and their upcoming appointment
#    POST /my-space/cancel        cancels the appointment SON
#    GE T /my-accou              nt account modification form
#    POST /my-accoun              t update
#    POST /my-account/delete      delete account (and its appointments)
#
# Golden rule for this module: the patient in question is TOUJOURS, the one associated with the token
# (outils.patient_connecte), never an identifier sent by the browser. A
# patient can therefore neither view, modify, nor cancel anything belonging to another
# patient, even by crafting their own requests.
#
# Any modification or deletion of the account requires the password ACTUEL:
# Someone who finds a session that has been left open cannot change the
# nor delete the account. Incorrect entries of the current password are
# counted as login failures (same limit).
#
# Security: All of these URL are reserved for the USER role (rule ^/my-
# security/acces.py).
# =========================================================================

from django.contrib import messages
from django.shortcuts import redirect, render
from django.utils.translation import gettext as _, ngettext
from django.views.decorators.http import require_GET, require_http_methods, require_POST

from metier.erreurs import MetierErreur
from modeles.models import Client
from securite import auth, limiteur

from .. import outils
from ..application import application
from ..formulaires import MonCompteForm
from ..modeles_vues import RendezVousVue
from .agenda import url_agenda
from .personnes import CHAMPS_ERREURS_METIER


# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# GET /my-space
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
@require_GET
def espace(request):
    patient = outils.patient_connecte(request)
    rendez_vous = [RendezVousVue(
        rv.id,
        outils.formater_jour(rv.jour),
        rv.creneau.horaire(),
        rv.creneau.medecin.libelle(),
         # link to the doctor’s schedule for that day: the patient sees their name there
        url_agenda(rv.creneau.medecin_id, rv.jour))
        for rv in application().get_rv_a_venir_client(patient.id)]
    return render(request, "espace.html", {"titre_page": _("Mon espace"),
                                           "patient": patient.libelle(), "rendez_vous": rendez_vous})


# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# POST /my-space/cancel f  ield: idRv
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
@require_POST
def annuler_rv(request):
    patient = outils.patient_connecte(request)
    id_rv = outils.entier_positif(request.POST.get("idRv"))
    rv = application().get_rv_by_id(id_rv) if id_rv is not None else None
     # a nonexistent appointment, and one for a AUTRE patient, receive the same
     # response: no information is disclosed about other patients’ appointments
    if rv is None or rv.client_id != patient.id:
        messages.error(request, _("Ce rendez-vous n'existe pas (ou plus)."))
    else:
        application().supprimer_rv(rv)
        messages.success(request, _("Rendez-vous annulé."))
    return redirect("espace")


# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# GET /my-account: the form, pre-filled with the patient’s information;
# POST /my-account: the update
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
@require_http_methods(["GET", "POST"])
def compte(request):
    patient = outils.patient_connecte(request)
    if request.method == "GET":
        return page(request, MonCompteForm(initial={
            "titre": patient.titre, "prenom": patient.prenom, "nom": patient.nom,
            "login": patient.compte.login, "version": patient.version}))
    formulaire = MonCompteForm(request.POST)
    if not formulaire.is_valid():
        return page(request, formulaire)
     # the current password; false: the message goes to SOUS the field (an error added
     # to the field by add_error), and at the bottom of the page
    erreur = verifier_mot_de_passe_actuel(request, patient, formulaire.cleaned_data["current_password"])
    if erreur is not None:
        formulaire.add_error("current_password", erreur)
        return page(request, formulaire, erreur)
    try:
        client = application().modifier_client(patient.id, formulaire.donnees())
    except MetierErreur as e:
        return page(request, formulaire, e.message, CHAMPS_ERREURS_METIER.get(e.code, []))
     # the login and display name are DANS the token: a new one is issued; otherwise
     # the navigation bar would retain the old name
    messages.success(request, _("Votre compte a été modifié."))
    return auth.poser_jeton(redirect("espace"), client.compte)


# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# POST /my-account/delete f  ield: current_password
# The account, the client, and TOUS their appointments all disappear together, then the
# The patient is disconnected.
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
@require_POST
def supprimer_compte(request):
    patient = outils.patient_connecte(request)
    erreur = verifier_mot_de_passe_actuel(request, patient, request.POST.get("current_password", ""))
    if erreur is not None:
        messages.error(request, erreur)
        return redirect("compte")
    application().supprimer_client(patient.id)
    messages.success(request, _("Votre compte a été supprimé."))
    return auth.effacer_jeton(redirect("login"))


# ----------------------------------------------------------------- internal functions
# the account page; a form was rejected: code 422
def page(request, formulaire, erreur=None, champs_invalides=()):
    refuse = erreur is not None or (formulaire.is_bound and bool(formulaire.errors))
    return render(request, "compte.html", {
        "titre_page": _("Gérer mon compte"),
        "formulaire": formulaire.signaler(champs_invalides), "erreur": erreur,
    }, status=422 if refuse else 200)


# None if the current password is correct; otherwise, the error message
def verifier_mot_de_passe_actuel(request, patient: Client, mot_de_passe: str) -> str | None:
    ip = outils.ip(request)
    login = patient.compte.login
    minutes = limiteur.minutes_blocage_login(ip, login)
    if minutes > 0:
        return ngettext("Trop de tentatives infructueuses. Réessayez dans %(minutes)d minute.",
                        "Trop de tentatives infructueuses. Réessayez dans %(minutes)d minutes.",
                        minutes) % {"minutes": minutes}
    if not mot_de_passe or auth.valider(login, mot_de_passe) is None:
        limiteur.echec_login(ip, login)
        return _("Mot de passe actuel incorrect.")
    return None

    The patient’s personal pages. The golden rule of this module: the patient in question is always the one associated with the token ([outils.patient_connecte]), never an identifier sent by the browser. A patient cannot therefore view, modify, or cancel information belonging to another patient, even if they generate their own requests.

    • Lines 46–58: My Space: the patient’s name and their upcoming appointments, formatted ([RendezVousVue]), each with a link to the doctor’s schedule for that day. The function [url_agenda] is part of the calendar module (line 39, [from .agenda import url_agenda]);
    • lines 64–76: the cancellation of his appointment. Both a nonexistent appointment and another patient’s appointment receive the same response: no information is disclosed about other patients’ appointments (not even their existence);
    • lines 83–92: the “Manage My Account” form, pre-filled with the patient’s information, and its submission;
    • lines 95–106: the modification. Any modification requires the current password: someone who found a session left open would be unable to change the password or do anything else. If the current password is incorrect, the form is redisplayed, with the message below the field and at the bottom of the page. [add_error(champ, message)] adds an error to a field, as if validation had detected it (example 19). After the modification, a new token is generated: the login and the displayed name are included in the token, and the navigation bar would otherwise retain the old name until the next login;
    • lines 114–123: deletion of the account, the client, and all their appointments, using the same business-logic method as for the administrator. This second form on the page is hand-coded (a single field: the current password). The patient is then logged out (the token cookie is cleared);
    • lines 137–148: Verification of the current password. This is subject to the attempt limiter, just like a login: without this, someone with an open session could try thousands of passwords via the “Manage My Account” form and discover the correct one.

    <!doctype html>
{% comment %}
  =========================================================================
  templates/layout.html
  -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Le gabarit PARENT de toutes les pages (cf. exemple 15) : chaque page
  (agenda.html, login.html...) l'ÉTEND ({% extends %}) et remplit son bloc
  [contenu].

  Django ÉCHAPPE tout ce qu'il affiche avec {{ ... }} (les caractères < > & " '
  deviennent &lt; &gt;...) : protection contre l'injection de HTML via un nom
  saisi, par exemple. Pour insérer du HTML tel quel, il faut le demander
  explicitement (filtre safe, cf. fragments/captcha.html).

  Messages : un succès s'affiche en HAUT de la page, une erreur en BAS, sur fond
  rose léger (balises zone_succes et zone_erreurs, cf. web/templatetags/rdv.py).

  Le gabarit partage les variables de la page : [titre_page] (le titre de la
  page, transmis par la vue, déjà traduit). LANGUAGE_CODE : la langue de la
  requête (cf. web/middleware.py).
  =========================================================================
{% endcomment %}
{% load static i18n rdv %}
<html lang="{{ LANGUAGE_CODE }}">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
  <title>{{ titre_page }} - RdvMedecins</title>
  {# static: the URL from a file in the static folder #}
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="{% static 'lib/bootstrap/css/bootstrap.min.css' %}">
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="{% static 'css/styles.css' %}">
</head>
<body>
  <div class="container py-4">
    {% include "fragments/navbar.html" %}
    {% zone_succes %}
    <main>
      {% block contenu %}{% endblock %}
    </main>
    {% zone_erreurs %}
  </div>
  {# the "Are you sure?" window, hidden until needed #}
  {% include "fragments/confirmation.html" %}
  <script src="{% static 'js/app.js' %}"></script>
</body>
</html>

    The parent template for all pages (Example 15): each page extends it ([{% extends "layout.html" %}]) and fills in its [contenu] block (line 38).

    • Line 23: the tag libraries used: [static] (static files), [i18n] (translations, Example 22), and [rdv], ours (web layer, above). A parent template does not pass its libraries on to the templates that extend it: each page loads the ones it needs;
    • line 24: the page’s language, [fr] or [en]: the active language of the request, set by the [FixerLangue] middleware;
    • line 28: the page title, already translated by the view, which passes it in the variable [titre_page];
    • lines 30–31: the [{% static %}] tag renders the URL from a file in the [static] folder (Example 15);
    • lines 35–40: the navigation bar, the success messages at the top of the page, the page content, and the error area at the bottom of the page. The navigation bar snippet is inserted by [{% include %}] (Example 15): it accesses the page’s variables. The two message areas are the inclusion tags from [web/templatetags/rdv.py];
    • lines 43–44: the “Are you sure?” window, hidden until needed, and the script that displays it.

    The header comment (lines 2–22) is a [{% comment %}] tag: a template comment that can span multiple lines ([{# ... #}] fits on a single line, example 14). It is written after [<!doctype html>]: the first line of the sent page must be the document type declaration. The DTL escapes everything it displays using [{{ ... }}] (Example 14): a user-entered name containing HTML ([<script>]) is displayed as-is, without being interpreted. This prevents HTML (XSS) from being injected effortlessly into all pages.

    {% comment %}
  =========================================================================
  templates/fragments/navbar.html - la barre de navigation.

  Titre, FR/EN, rôle, nom, déconnexion - et le menu, dont les entrées dépendent
  du rôle : elles sont calculées par le processeur de contexte web/contextes.py
  (variable menu), avec, pour chacune, son URL, son libellé, et si elle est celle
  de la page courante (classe "active").

  utilisateur : l'utilisateur connecté, ou None (cf. web/contextes.py).
  =========================================================================
{% endcomment %}
{% load i18n %}
<nav class="navbar navbar-expand-sm navbar-dark bg-primary rounded mb-4 px-3">
  <span class="navbar-brand mb-0">RdvMedecins</span>

  <ul class="navbar-nav me-auto">
    {% for entree in menu %}
    <li class="nav-item">
      <a class="nav-link{% if entree.active %} active{% endif %}" href="{{ entree.url }}">{{ entree.libelle }}</a>
    </li>
    {% endfor %}
  </ul>

  <div class="d-flex align-items-center gap-2">
    {# FR / EN: simple links (GET /language/fr), with the active language highlighted #}
    {% get_available_languages as langues %}
    <div class="btn-group btn-group-sm" role="group" aria-label="FR / EN">
      {% for code, nom in langues %}
      <a class="btn {% if code == LANGUAGE_CODE %}btn-light{% else %}btn-outline-light{% endif %}"
         href="{% url 'langue' code %}">{{ code|upper }}</a>
      {% endfor %}
    </div>

    {% if utilisateur %}
    <span class="badge text-bg-light text-primary">{{ utilisateur.role }}</span>
    <span class="text-white">{{ utilisateur.nom }}</span>
    {# Logout is a POST: a form reduced to its button (and the anti-CSRF token) #}
    <form method="post" action="{% url 'logout' %}" class="m-0">
      {% csrf_token %}
      <button type="submit" class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-light">{% translate "Se déconnecter" %}</button>
    </form>
    {% endif %}
  </div>
</nav>

    The navigation bar. It simply displays what the [web/contextes.py] context processor has prepared: the logged-in user ([utilisateur]), and the menu items ([menu]), which depend on the role.

    • lines 17–23: the menu, with each entry having its own URL and label; the [active] class of [Bootstrap] highlights the entry for the currently displayed page;
    • Lines 27–32: the FR / EN buttons, simple links ([/langue/fr]), with the active language highlighted. [{% get_available_languages as langues %}] (library [i18n]) stores the setting [LANGUAGES]—a list of (code, name) pairs—in the variable [langues], which the loop unpacks ([{% for code, nom in langues %}]); the filter [upper] capitalizes the code. [{% url 'langue' code %}] creates URL for a route that has a parameter (example 15);
    • Lines 35–43: For a logged-in user, their role, name, and the logout button. Logout is a request for POST: a form reduced to just its button, with its anti-CSRF token ([{% csrf_token %}], Example 21).

    {% comment %}
  =========================================================================
  templates/fragments/confirmation.html - la fenêtre modale "Êtes-vous sûr ?"
  (cf. exemple 21).

  Elle remplace la boîte window.confirm() du navigateur, qu'on ne peut ni mettre
  en forme, ni traduire (ses boutons restent dans la langue du navigateur, pas
  dans celle de la page).

  Une SEULE fenêtre pour toute la page, cachée (d-none) au départ. Ses libellés
  sont traduits ici, par le serveur, comme le reste de la page ; le petit script
  static/js/app.js se contente de l'afficher, d'y placer le message propre au
  formulaire (attribut data-confirmation), et d'envoyer le formulaire si
  l'utilisateur confirme.
  =========================================================================
{% endcomment %}
{% load i18n %}
<div id="modale-confirmation" class="d-none">
  <div class="modal-backdrop fade show"></div>
  <div class="modal fade show d-block" tabindex="-1" role="alertdialog" aria-modal="true"
       aria-labelledby="modale-confirmation-titre" aria-describedby="modale-confirmation-message">
    <div class="modal-dialog modal-dialog-centered">
      <div class="modal-content">
        <div class="modal-header">
          <h5 class="modal-title" id="modale-confirmation-titre">{% translate "Confirmation" %}</h5>
          <button type="button" class="btn-close" data-action="non" aria-label="{% translate 'Fermer' %}"></button>
        </div>
        <div class="modal-body">
          <p class="mb-0" id="modale-confirmation-message"></p>
        </div>
        <div class="modal-footer">
          {# "No, go back" instead of "Cancel": the question is sometimes "Cancel this appointment?" #}
          <button type="button" class="btn btn-secondary" data-action="non">{% translate "Non, revenir" %}</button>
          <button type="button" class="btn btn-danger" data-action="oui">{% translate "Oui, confirmer" %}</button>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>

    The “Are you sure?” modal window from Example 21, which replaces the browser’s [window.confirm()] dialog box: this dialog box does not format correctly, and its buttons remain in the browser’s language, not the page’s language. A single window for the entire page, initially hidden (class [d-none] derived from [Bootstrap]); its labels are translated by the server, just like the rest of the page. The [static/js/app.js] script displays it, places the message from the form to be confirmed inside it (its [data-confirmation] attribute), and submits the form if the user confirms. The "Cancel" button is labeled “No, go back” rather than “Cancel”: the question is sometimes “Cancel this appointment?”, and a “Cancel” button would be ambiguous in that context. The attributes [role="alertdialog"], [aria-modal], [aria-labelledby], and [aria-describedby] describe the window to screen readers: a dialog box awaiting a response, its title, and its message.

    {% comment %}
  =========================================================================
  templates/fragments/reservation.html - la fenêtre de réservation de l'agenda.

  Les VRAIES classes Bootstrap d'une fenêtre modale (.modal, .modal-backdrop...),
  rendues visibles "en dur" (show d-block) plutôt que par le JavaScript de
  Bootstrap. C'est le SERVEUR qui décide de l'afficher (paramètre &reserver=... de
  l'URL), et la fermer revient à suivre un lien vers la même page sans ce
  paramètre.

  Le fragment lit directement les variables de la page qui l'insère
  (reservation, id_medecin, jour, url_retour).
  =========================================================================
{% endcomment %}
{% load i18n %}
<div class="modal-backdrop fade show"></div>
<div class="modal fade show d-block" tabindex="-1" role="dialog" aria-modal="true" aria-labelledby="titre-reservation">
  <div class="modal-dialog modal-dialog-centered">
    <form method="post" action="{% url 'agenda_reserver' %}" class="modal-content">
      <div class="modal-header">
        <h5 class="modal-title" id="titre-reservation">{% translate "Réserver ce créneau" %}</h5>
        <a class="btn-close" href="{{ url_retour }}" aria-label="{% translate 'Fermer' %}"></a>
      </div>

      <div class="modal-body">
        <p>{% blocktranslate with horaire=reservation.horaire %}Créneau de {{ horaire }}{% endblocktranslate %}</p>

        {# what the server needs to know in addition to the selected patient #}
        {% csrf_token %}
        <input type="hidden" name="idMedecin" value="{{ id_medecin }}">
        <input type="hidden" name="jour" value="{{ jour }}">
        <input type="hidden" name="idCreneau" value="{{ reservation.id_creneau }}">

        {# A patient is booking for themselves: no list to choose from (and the server ignores any idClient anyway) #}
        {% if reservation.patient %}
        <p class="mb-0">
          <span>{% translate "Patient" %}</span> :
          <strong>{{ reservation.patient }}</strong>
        </p>
        {% else %}
        <label class="form-label" for="idClient">{% translate "Patient" %}</label>
        <select id="idClient" name="idClient" class="form-select" required autofocus>
          <option value="">{% translate "-- choisir un patient --" %}</option>
          {% for client in reservation.clients %}
          <option value="{{ client.id }}">{{ client.libelle }}</option>
          {% endfor %}
        </select>
        {% endif %}
      </div>

      <div class="modal-footer">
        <a class="btn btn-secondary" href="{{ url_retour }}">{% translate "Annuler" %}</a>
        <button type="submit" class="btn btn-primary">{% translate "Confirmer" %}</button>
      </div>
    </form>
  </div>
</div>

    The calendar booking window. It uses the actual classes of a modal window from [Bootstrap] ([modal], [modal-backdrop]...), but made visible "hard-coded" ([show d-block]), rather than via the [JavaScript] from [Bootstrap]: it is the server that decides to display it when URL contains [&reserver=...]. Closing it (using the X or the Cancel button) is equivalent to following a link to the same page without that parameter ([url_retour]).

    • Line 26: [{% blocktranslate with horaire=reservation.horaire %}]: a translated text that contains a variable (example 22). In a [blocktranslate], only simple variables are allowed ([{{ horaire }}], not [{{ reservation.horaire }}]): the [with] clause creates one;
    • lines 29–32: the anti-CSRF token, and what the server needs to know: the doctor, the day, and the time slot;
    • lines 35–48: a patient makes a reservation for themselves: their name, with no list to choose from (and the server ignores any [idClient] field anyway). The administrator and doctors select the patient from a list; [required] and [autofocus]: the browser requires a selection and places the cursor in the list.

    {% comment %}
  =========================================================================
  templates/fragments/captcha.html - le captcha de la page d'authentification
  (cf. securite/captchas.py). Il protège à la fois la connexion et l'accès à la
  création de compte (bouton "Créer un compte client"). Il lit la variable
  [captcha] de la page.

  captcha.svg|safe : l'image SVG est insérée TELLE QUELLE dans la page, sans
  échappement. C'est sans danger ici parce que ce SVG est fabriqué par le serveur
  lui-même et ne contient rien qui vienne de l'utilisateur - on ne ferait JAMAIS
  cela avec une saisie.

  Le champ caché captcha_id dit au serveur QUEL captcha vérifier ; la bonne
  réponse, elle, n'est jamais envoyée au navigateur. "Autre image" recharge
  simplement la page ({% url 'login' %} : l'URL de la page, sans ses paramètres).
  =========================================================================
{% endcomment %}
{% load i18n %}
<div class="mb-3">
  <label class="form-label" for="captcha">{% translate "Recopiez les caractères de l'image" %}</label>
  <div class="d-flex align-items-center gap-3 mb-2">
    <div class="captcha-image" role="img" aria-label="{% translate 'Image de vérification anti-robots' %}">{{ captcha.svg|safe }}</div>
    <a class="small" href="{% url 'login' %}">{% translate "Autre image" %}</a>
  </div>
  <input type="hidden" name="captcha_id" value="{{ captcha.id }}">
  <input id="captcha" name="captcha" type="text" maxlength="10" autocomplete="off" autocapitalize="off"
         spellcheck="false" required class="form-control">
  <div class="form-text">{% translate "Majuscules ou minuscules, peu importe." %}</div>
</div>

    The CAPTCHA (example 27). [captcha.svg|safe] inserts the image SVG as-is, without escaping it: otherwise, the browser would display its code XML. This is safe here because this SVG is generated by the server and contains nothing provided by the user: we would never do this with user input. The hidden field [captcha_id] tells the server which CAPTCHA to verify; the response itself is never sent to the browser. The “Other image” link reloads the login page—and thus the CAPTCHA. The attributes of the input fields ([autocomplete="off"], [autocapitalize="off"], [spellcheck="false"]) prevent the browser from suggesting a previous entry and the phone’s keyboard from capitalizing letters or correcting spelling.

    11.18.2.1. templates/forms/champ.html

     1

    {% comment %}
  templates/formulaires/champ.html - un champ complet d'un formulaire : libellé,
  zone de saisie, puis son message d'erreur ou son aide (cf. exemple 18 et le
  réglage FORM_RENDERER). La zone de saisie est encadrée en rouge (classe
  is-invalid) par la méthode signaler du formulaire (cf. web/formulaires.py).
{% endcomment %}
<div class="mb-3">
  <label class="form-label" for="{{ field.id_for_label }}">{{ field.label }}</label>
  {{ field }}
  {% if field.errors %}<div class="invalid-feedback d-block" id="{{ field.auto_id }}_error">{% for erreur in field.errors %}{{ erreur }}{% if not forloop.last %}<br>{% endif %}{% endfor %}</div>{% endif %}
  {% if field.help_text and not field.errors %}<div class="form-text" id="{{ field.auto_id }}_helptext">{{ field.help_text }}</div>{% endif %}
</div>

    The template for a complete field—that of the [RenduBootstrap] rendering engine (web layer, above)—as shown in Example 18: the label, the input field ([{{ field }}], with the classes CSS provided by the form), followed by the error message or, if none, the help text. The classes [invalid-feedback] (the message in red) and [form-text] (the help text in gray) are those of [Bootstrap]; [d-block] displays the message even if the input field is not immediately preceding it. A field may have multiple errors: they are separated by a line break ([forloop.last], example 14).

    The identifiers [..._error] and [..._helptext] are not chosen at random: these are the ones that [Django] refers to in the [aria-describedby] attributes of the input field, with [aria-invalid] for a field with an error. A screen reader thus reads the error message or help text along with the field:

    1
2
3
4
5
    <div class="mb-3">
  <label class="form-label" for="id_prenom">Prénom</label>
  <input type="text" name="prenom" maxlength="20" class="form-control is-invalid" required aria-invalid="true" aria-describedby="id_prenom_error" id="id_prenom">
  <div class="invalid-feedback d-block" id="id_prenom_error">Le prénom est obligatoire.</div>
</div>

    The red border ([is-invalid]) was added by the form’s [signaler] method; [maxlength] and [required] by [Django], based on the field’s options. The [required] attribute does not prevent an empty form from being submitted: the application’s forms carry the [novalidate] attribute (see below); validation is performed by the server.

    {% extends "layout.html" %}
{% comment %}
  =========================================================================
  templates/login.html - le formulaire de connexion (cf. web/vues/auth.py).
  Un <form> HTML ordinaire, écrit à la main : le navigateur envoie lui-même login,
  mot de passe et réponse au captcha en POST /login, sans JavaScript. En cas
  d'échec, le serveur renvoie CETTE page, avec le login déjà saisi, un NOUVEAU
  captcha et l'erreur, affichée en bas de page par le gabarit parent.
  =========================================================================
{% endcomment %}
{% load i18n %}

{% block contenu %}
<div class="row justify-content-center">
  <div class="col-sm-8 col-md-6 col-lg-5">
    <div class="card p-4">
      <h5 class="card-title mb-3">{% translate "Connexion" %}</h5>

      <form method="post" action="{% url 'login' %}">
        {% csrf_token %}
        <div class="mb-3">
          <label class="form-label" for="login">{% translate "Login" %}</label>
          {# autofocus: a Boolean attribute, set if the condition is true. The cursor goes to the first field to be filled in #}
          <input id="login" name="login" type="text" class="form-control" autocomplete="username"
                 value="{{ login }}" required{% if not login %} autofocus{% endif %}>
        </div>
        <div class="mb-3">
          <label class="form-label" for="password">{% translate "Mot de passe" %}</label>
          <input id="password" name="password" type="password" class="form-control"
                 autocomplete="current-password" required{% if login %} autofocus{% endif %}>
        </div>

        {% include "fragments/captcha.html" %}

        <button type="submit" class="btn btn-primary w-100">{% translate "Se connecter" %}</button>

        {% comment %}
          pas encore de compte : un patient peut en créer un lui-même. Ce n'est PAS
          un simple lien : c'est un second bouton d'envoi de CE formulaire, qui part
          vers une autre adresse (formaction). Le serveur y vérifie le captcha
          ci-dessus avant d'ouvrir la page de création de compte (cf.
          web/vues/inscription.py). formnovalidate : le navigateur n'exige pas
          login et mot de passe (inutiles pour créer un compte). Entrée dans un
          champ déclenche toujours le PREMIER bouton du formulaire, "Se connecter".
        {% endcomment %}
        <button type="submit" class="btn btn-outline-primary w-100 mt-3"
                formaction="{% url 'inscription_acces' %}" formnovalidate>{% translate "Créer un compte client" %}</button>
        <div class="form-text text-center">{% translate "Pour créer un compte, recopiez d'abord les caractères de l'image." %}</div>
      </form>

      <div class="text-muted small mt-3">
        <span>{% translate "Comptes de démonstration (mot de passe = login) :" %}</span>
        <ul class="mb-0 mt-1">
          <li><code>admin</code> - <span>{% translate "rôle ADMIN : rendez-vous + gestion des médecins et des clients" %}</span></li>
          <li><code>pelissier</code>, <code>tatou</code>, <code>dupont</code> - <span>{% translate "rôle DOCTOR : prise et annulation de rendez-vous" %}</span></li>
          <li><code>martin</code>, <code>durand</code>, <code>bistrou</code>, <code>german</code> - <span>{% translate "rôle USER (patients) : réservation pour eux-mêmes, gestion de leur compte" %}</span></li>
        </ul>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
{% endblock %}

    The login form, a hand-coded [<form>], is sent via POST to [/login]. The [{% extends %}] tag is the first in the template (line 1), as required by DTL; the comment follows.

    • Lines 24–30: The entered login is redisplayed after a failed attempt ([login]). The attribute [autofocus] places the cursor in the first field to be filled in: the username if it is empty, the password otherwise (after a failed login attempt or after creating an account). A Boolean attribute is either present or absent: [{% if not login %} autofocus{% endif %}];
    • line 33: the CAPTCHA;
    • lines 46–47: the “Create a Customer Account” button is not a link; it is a second button that submits the same form to a different address (button attribute [formaction]). The server verifies the CAPTCHA there before opening the account creation page ([inscription.acces]). [formnovalidate]: The browser does not require a username and password (attributes [required]), as they are not needed to create an account. Pressing the Enter key in a field always triggers the first form submission button: Log In;
    • lines 51–58: demo accounts, for testing.

    {% extends "layout.html" %}
{% comment %}
  =========================================================================
  templates/agenda.html - la page principale (cf. web/vues/agenda.py).
  Trois blocs :
    1. le choix du médecin et du jour ;
    2. l'agenda ;
    3. la fenêtre de réservation (fragment reservation).
  Une éventuelle erreur (date invalide, médecin inconnu) est affichée en bas de
  la page par le gabarit parent (balise zone_erreurs).
  =========================================================================
{% endcomment %}
{% load i18n %}

{% block contenu %}
  {# 1. Selecting a doctor and date: a GET form, which simply reloads this page with ?idMedecin=...&day=... #}
  <form method="get" action="{% url 'agenda' %}" class="card p-3 mb-3">
    <div class="row g-2 align-items-end">
      <div class="col-sm-5">
        <label class="form-label" for="idMedecin">{% translate "Médecin" %}</label>
        <select id="idMedecin" name="idMedecin" class="form-select" required>
          <option value="">{% translate "-- choisir un médecin --" %}</option>
          {% for medecin in medecins %}
          <option value="{{ medecin.id }}"{% if medecin.selectionne %} selected{% endif %}>{{ medecin.libelle }}</option>
          {% endfor %}
        </select>
      </div>
      <div class="col-sm-4">
        <label class="form-label" for="jour">{% translate "Jour" %}</label>
        <input id="jour" name="jour" type="date" class="form-control" value="{{ jour }}" required>
      </div>
      <div class="col-sm-3">
        <button type="submit" class="btn btn-primary w-100">{% translate "Voir l'agenda" %}</button>
      </div>
    </div>
  </form>

  {# Patient who already has an upcoming appointment: why there is no “Book” button #}
  {% if info %}
  <div class="alert alert-info">
    <span>{{ info }}</span>
    <a href="{% url 'espace' %}" class="alert-link">{% translate "Mon espace" %}</a>
  </div>
  {% endif %}

  {# 2. The calendar #}
  {% if agenda %}
  <div class="card p-3">
    <h5>{% translate "Agenda du" %} {{ agenda.jour }} - {{ agenda.medecin }}</h5>

    {% if agenda.lignes %}
    <table class="table table-hover align-middle">
      <thead>
        <tr>
          <th>{% translate "Créneau" %}</th>
          <th>{% translate "Statut" %}</th>
          <th></th>
        </tr>
      </thead>
      <tbody>
        {% for ligne in agenda.lignes %}
        <tr{% if ligne.reservable %} class="creneau-libre"{% endif %}>
          <td>{{ ligne.horaire }}</td>
          <td>
            {% comment %}
              [patient] n'est renseigné que si l'utilisateur a le droit de voir ce
              nom (ADMIN, DOCTOR, ou le patient pour SON rendez-vous) - sinon,
              simplement « Réservé »
            {% endcomment %}
            {% if ligne.libre %}
            <span class="badge text-bg-success">{% translate "Libre" %}</span>
            {% elif ligne.patient %}
            <span class="badge {% if ligne.moi %}text-bg-primary{% else %}text-bg-secondary{% endif %}">{{ ligne.patient }}</span>
            {% else %}
            <span class="badge text-bg-secondary">{% translate "Réservé" %}</span>
            {% endif %}
          </td>
          <td>
            {% comment %}
              les boutons affichés ont été décidés par la vue (reservable, id_rv)
              selon le rôle de l'utilisateur. "Réserver" est un simple lien : il
              rouvre cette page avec la fenêtre de réservation de ce créneau
            {% endcomment %}
            {% if ligne.reservable %}
            <a class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-success" href="{{ ligne.url_reserver }}">{% translate "Réserver" %}</a>
            {% endif %}
            {# "Cancel" MODIFIE data: so it’s a POST #}
            {% if ligne.id_rv %}
            <form method="post" action="{% url 'agenda_annuler' %}" class="m-0"
                  data-confirmation="{% translate 'Annuler ce rendez-vous ?' %}">
              {% csrf_token %}
              <input type="hidden" name="idRv" value="{{ ligne.id_rv }}">
              <input type="hidden" name="idMedecin" value="{{ id_medecin }}">
              <input type="hidden" name="jour" value="{{ jour }}">
              <button type="submit" class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-danger">{% translate "Annuler" %}</button>
            </form>
            {% endif %}
          </td>
        </tr>
        {% endfor %}
      </tbody>
    </table>
    {% else %}
    <p class="text-muted mb-0">{% translate "Ce médecin n'a aucun créneau horaire." %}</p>
    {% endif %}
  </div>
  {% else %}
  <p class="text-muted">{% translate "Choisissez un médecin et un jour, puis cliquez sur « Voir l'agenda »." %}</p>
  {% endif %}

  {# 3. The booking window, only if the URL contains &reserver=... #}
  {% if reservation %}
  {% include "fragments/reservation.html" %}
  {% endif %}
{% endblock %}

    The main page. Three sections: selecting a doctor and a day, the calendar, and the booking window.

    • Lines 17–36: Selecting a doctor and a day: a GET form (example 17), which reloads the page with [?idMedecin=...&jour=...] in the URL. The day is a [type="date"] field: the browser displays a calendar and sends the date in [aaaa-mm-jj] format, regardless of how it displays it ([30/09/2026] in French); the initial value ([value]) is written in this same format;
    • lines 39–44: for a patient who already has an upcoming appointment, why isn’t there a “Book” button with a link to “My Account”?
    • Lines 70–76: The slot status: Available (in green), the patient’s name (in blue for an appointment booked by the logged-in patient, in gray otherwise), or “Reserved.” The template does not determine anything: [ligne.patient] is only displayed if the user has permission to view that name;
    • lines 84–86: “Reserve” is a simple link: it reopens the page with the reservation window for that time slot ([ligne.url_reserver]). It does not modify anything: a GET is sufficient;
    • lines 88–97: “Cancel” modifies data: it is a POST form (example 21), with its anti-CSRF token, the appointment to be canceled, and information to return to the same page (the doctor, the day). The [data-confirmation] attribute causes the page’s script to request confirmation; its text is represented by [{% translate %}], enclosed in single quotes within the attribute, which is itself enclosed in double quotes;
    • lines 112–114: the booking window, if URL requests it (and if the time slot is bookable).

    {% extends "layout.html" %}
{% comment %}
  =========================================================================
  templates/personnes/liste.html - la liste des médecins OU des clients (ADMIN).
  Un seul gabarit pour les deux : les textes propres à chacun arrivent dans
  [textes], et [section] ("medecins" ou "clients") donne le début des noms des
  routes (cf. web/vues/personnes.py).
  =========================================================================
{% endcomment %}
{% load i18n %}

{% block contenu %}
  <div class="d-flex justify-content-between align-items-center mb-3">
    <h4 class="mb-0">{{ textes.titre }}</h4>
    <a class="btn btn-primary" href="{{ url_ajout }}">{{ textes.ajouter }}</a>
  </div>

  <div class="card p-3">
    {% if personnes %}
    <table class="table table-hover align-middle mb-0">
      <thead>
        <tr>
          <th>{% translate "Titre" %}</th>
          <th>{% translate "Prénom" %}</th>
          <th>{% translate "Nom" %}</th>
          <th>{% translate "Login" %}</th>
          <th></th>
        </tr>
      </thead>
      <tbody>
        {# personne.compte.login: the account, loaded by the same request (select_related) #}
        {% for personne in personnes %}
        <tr>
          <td>{{ personne.titre }}</td>
          <td>{{ personne.prenom }}</td>
          <td>{{ personne.nom }}</td>
          <td><code>{{ personne.compte.login }}</code></td>
          <td class="text-end">
            <div class="d-inline-flex gap-2">
              {# section|add:"_modification": "medecins_modification", the route name #}
              <a class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-primary"
                 href="{% url section|add:'_modification' personne.id %}">{% translate "Modifier" %}</a>
              {# data-confirmation: a confirmation window will open before the form is submitted (see static/js/app.js) #}
              <form method="post" action="{% url section|add:'_supprimer' personne.id %}" class="m-0"
                    data-confirmation="{{ textes.confirmer_suppression }}">
                {% csrf_token %}
                <button type="submit" class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-danger">{% translate "Supprimer" %}</button>
              </form>
            </div>
          </td>
        </tr>
        {% endfor %}
      </tbody>
    </table>
    {% else %}
    <p class="text-muted mb-0">{{ textes.vide }}</p>
    {% endif %}
  </div>
{% endblock %}

    The list of doctors or clients: the text specific to each one is stored in the variable [textes], and the route names are generated from the section name: [section|add:'_modification'] yields [medecins_modification] or [clients_modification] (the filter [add] adds two numbers or, as in this case, concatenates two strings). [{% url %}] thus accepts, as a route name, a calculated expression followed by the route parameters ([personne.id]). [personne.compte.login]: the account login, loaded along with the list (layer DAO), and stored with it in the cache. The Delete button is a POST form, with confirmation.

    {% extends "layout.html" %}
{% comment %}
  =========================================================================
  templates/personnes/formulaire.html - création OU modification d'un médecin ou
  d'un client (ADMIN), avec le formulaire PersonneForm.

  Quand la saisie est refusée (champ vide, login déjà pris...), la vue réaffiche
  CETTE page, et le gabarit montre :
    - les valeurs déjà saisies (sauf le mot de passe) ;
    - les champs fautifs encadrés en rouge (classe Bootstrap "is-invalid") ;
    - sous un champ refusé par la validation, son message ;
    - le message d'erreur de la page, EN BAS de la page (balise zone_erreurs).
  Le formulaire est envoyé à l'URL de la page elle-même (pas d'attribut action).
  =========================================================================
{% endcomment %}
{% load i18n %}

{% block contenu %}
<div class="row justify-content-center">
  <div class="col-md-8 col-lg-6">
    <div class="card p-4">
      <h5 class="card-title mb-3">{{ titre_page }}</h5>

      <form method="post" novalidate>
        {% csrf_token %}
        {# title, first name, last name: a section common to three forms #}
        {% include "macros.html#identite" %}

        <h6 class="mt-4 text-muted">{% translate "Compte utilisateur" %}</h6>
        {{ formulaire.login.as_field_group }}
        {# never pre-filled: the password is never sent back to the browser #}
        {{ formulaire.password.as_field_group }}
        {# on edit only: the record version, in a hidden field (the optimistic lock) #}
        {% if formulaire.version %}{{ formulaire.version }}{% endif %}

        <div class="d-flex gap-2 mt-4">
          <button type="submit" class="btn btn-primary">{% translate "Enregistrer" %}</button>
          <a class="btn btn-secondary" href="{{ url_liste }}">{% translate "Retour à la liste" %}</a>
        </div>
      </form>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
{% endblock %}

    Creating or modifying a doctor or a client using the [PersonneForm] form.

    • Line 24: a POST form without the [action] attribute: it is sent to the URL of the page itself ([/medecins/ajouter] or [/medecins/3/modifier]). [novalidate] disables browser validation ([required], [maxlength]...) when the form is submitted: the server performs the validation, and its result is authoritative (example 19);
    • line 27: title, first name, and last name, via the fragment [identite];
    • lines 30–32: the username and password, which are never pre-filled. Their tooltips differ between creation and modification (depending on the form builder);
    • line 34: for editing only, the hidden version field (the optimistic lock). [{{ formulaire.version }}] populates the input field alone, without a label: [<input type="hidden" name="version" value="1" id="id_version">]. When creating a record, the form does not have a [version] field: the variable is empty, and the test evaluates to false.

    Errors in the form itself that do not involve any fields ([non_field_errors], example 19) do not need to be displayed: the form does not generate any, and an invalid anti-CSRF token is rejected before the view (the 419 page).

    {% extends "layout.html" %}
{% comment %}
  =========================================================================
  templates/inscription.html - "Créer un compte client" (page publique, cf.
  web/vues/inscription.py), avec le formulaire InscriptionForm. Mêmes champs
  d'identité que le formulaire de l'ADMIN (fragment identite), mais le login et le
  mot de passe sont obligatoires, avec confirmation. Pas de captcha ICI : on
  n'arrive sur cette page qu'après avoir recopié celui de la page
  d'authentification (bouton "Créer un compte client").
  =========================================================================
{% endcomment %}
{% load i18n %}

{% block contenu %}
<div class="row justify-content-center">
  <div class="col-md-8 col-lg-6">
    <div class="card p-4">
      <h5 class="card-title mb-1">{% translate "Créer un compte client" %}</h5>
      <p class="text-muted small mb-3">{% translate "Ce compte vous permettra de prendre vous-même vos rendez-vous." %}</p>

      <form method="post" action="{% url 'inscription' %}" novalidate>
        {% csrf_token %}
        {% include "macros.html#identite" %}

        <h6 class="mt-4 text-muted">{% translate "Compte utilisateur" %}</h6>
        {{ formulaire.login.as_field_group }}
        {# The password and its confirmation, side by side #}
        <div class="row g-3">
          <div class="col-sm-6">{{ formulaire.password.as_field_group }}</div>
          <div class="col-sm-6">{{ formulaire.confirmation.as_field_group }}</div>
        </div>

        <div class="d-flex gap-2 mt-3">
          <button type="submit" class="btn btn-primary">{% translate "Créer mon compte" %}</button>
          <a class="btn btn-secondary" href="{% url 'login' %}">{% translate "Retour à la connexion" %}</a>
        </div>
      </form>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
{% endblock %}

    Creating a customer account: the identity fields, followed by the username, password, and password confirmation—all required fields—side by side (lines 28–31). The password help text specifies the minimum length: “At least 6 characters.” There is no CAPTCHA here: you can only reach this page after entering the CAPTCHA from the login page.

    {% extends "layout.html" %}
{% comment %}
  =========================================================================
  templates/espace.html - "Mon espace" : la page d'accueil du patient (rôle USER),
  affichée juste après sa connexion.
    - deux options : [Gérer mon compte] et [Voir un agenda] ;
    - son rendez-vous à venir, s'il en a un, avec le moyen de l'annuler.
  =========================================================================
{% endcomment %}
{% load i18n %}

{% block contenu %}
  <h4 class="mb-3">{% blocktranslate %}Bonjour {{ patient }}{% endblocktranslate %}</h4>

  <div class="row g-3 mb-4">
    <div class="col-sm-6">
      <a class="card p-4 h-100 text-decoration-none carte-option" href="{% url 'compte' %}">
        <h5 class="mb-1">{% translate "Gérer mon compte" %}</h5>
        <span class="text-muted">{% translate "Modifier mes informations, mon mot de passe, ou supprimer mon compte." %}</span>
      </a>
    </div>
    <div class="col-sm-6">
      <a class="card p-4 h-100 text-decoration-none carte-option" href="{% url 'agenda' %}">
        <h5 class="mb-1">{% translate "Voir un agenda" %}</h5>
        <span class="text-muted">{% translate "Consulter l'agenda d'un médecin et réserver un créneau." %}</span>
      </a>
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="card p-3">
    <h5>{% translate "Mon rendez-vous" %}</h5>
    {% comment %}
      normalement un seul (règle "un rendez-vous à venir à la fois"), mais la page
      sait en afficher plusieurs. {% for %} ... {% empty %} : une boucle, et ce
      qu'on affiche si la liste est vide ; forloop.last : dernier élément ?
    {% endcomment %}
    {% for rv in rendez_vous %}
    <div class="d-flex flex-wrap justify-content-between align-items-center gap-2 py-2{% if not forloop.last %} border-bottom{% endif %}">
      <div>
        <div class="fw-semibold">{{ rv.jour }}, {{ rv.horaire }}</div>
        <div class="text-muted">
          <span>{{ rv.medecin }}</span> -
          <a href="{{ rv.url_agenda }}">{% translate "voir dans l'agenda" %}</a>
        </div>
      </div>
      <form method="post" action="{% url 'espace_annuler' %}" class="m-0"
            data-confirmation="{% translate 'Annuler ce rendez-vous ?' %}">
        {% csrf_token %}
        <input type="hidden" name="idRv" value="{{ rv.id }}">
        <button type="submit" class="btn btn-outline-danger">{% translate "Annuler ce rendez-vous" %}</button>
      </form>
    </div>
    {% empty %}
    <p class="text-muted mb-0">{% translate "Vous n'avez aucun rendez-vous à venir." %}</p>
    {% endfor %}
  </div>
{% endblock %}

    “My Account,” the patient’s home page: two large cards (“Manage My Account,” “View Schedule”), and their upcoming appointment.

    • line 13: [{% blocktranslate %}Bonjour {{ patient }}{% endblocktranslate %}]: a translated text containing a variable ([Hello %(patient)s] in the English dictionary);
    • lines 37–55: [{% for %}] ... [{% empty %}] (Example 14) is a loop, followed by what to display if the list is empty. Normally, a patient has at most one upcoming appointment; however, the page is capable of displaying multiple appointments. [forloop.last] (Example 14): the last item has no separator;
    • lines 46–51: each appointment has a cancellation form (POST, with confirmation), which sends only its ID: the server will verify that it belongs to the logged-in patient.

    {% extends "layout.html" %}
{% comment %}
  =========================================================================
  templates/compte.html - "Gérer mon compte" (rôle USER). Deux formulaires
  indépendants sur la même page :
    1. la modification (identité, login, nouveau mot de passe facultatif), avec
       le formulaire MonCompteForm ;
    2. la suppression du compte - qui annule aussi ses rendez-vous : un
       formulaire écrit à la main.
  L'un comme l'autre exigent le mot de passe ACTUEL (champ current_password).
  =========================================================================
{% endcomment %}
{% load i18n %}

{% block contenu %}
<div class="row justify-content-center">
  <div class="col-md-8 col-lg-6">

    {# 1. edit; no validation: validation is performed by SERVEUR (see example 19) #}
    <div class="card p-4 mb-4">
      <h5 class="card-title mb-3">{% translate "Gérer mon compte" %}</h5>

      <form method="post" action="{% url 'compte' %}" novalidate>
        {% csrf_token %}
        {% include "macros.html#identite" %}

        <h6 class="mt-4 text-muted">{% translate "Compte utilisateur" %}</h6>
        {{ formulaire.login.as_field_group }}
        <div class="row g-3">
          <div class="col-sm-6">{{ formulaire.password.as_field_group }}</div>
          <div class="col-sm-6">{{ formulaire.confirmation.as_field_group }}</div>
        </div>
        {{ formulaire.current_password.as_field_group }}
        {# the record version: a hidden field (the optimistic lock) #}
        {{ formulaire.version }}

        <div class="d-flex gap-2 mt-4">
          <button type="submit" class="btn btn-primary">{% translate "Enregistrer" %}</button>
          <a class="btn btn-secondary" href="{% url 'espace' %}">{% translate "Retour à mon espace" %}</a>
        </div>
      </form>
    </div>

    {% comment %}
      2. suppression. Le champ du mot de passe a le même NOM que celui du premier
      formulaire (current_password), mais un autre id : deux éléments d'une même
      page ne peuvent pas avoir le même id
    {% endcomment %}
    <div class="card p-4 border-danger">
      <h5 class="card-title text-danger mb-1">{% translate "Supprimer mon compte" %}</h5>
      <p class="text-muted small">{% translate "Votre compte sera définitivement supprimé, ainsi que tous vos rendez-vous." %}</p>
      <form method="post" action="{% url 'compte_supprimer' %}" class="d-flex flex-wrap gap-2 align-items-end"
            data-confirmation="{% translate 'Supprimer définitivement votre compte ? Votre rendez-vous éventuel sera annulé.' %}">
        {% csrf_token %}
        <div class="flex-grow-1">
          <label class="form-label" for="mot_de_passe_suppression">{% translate "Mot de passe actuel" %}</label>
          <input id="mot_de_passe_suppression" name="current_password" type="password" maxlength="72"
                 autocomplete="current-password" required class="form-control">
        </div>
        <button type="submit" class="btn btn-danger">{% translate "Supprimer mon compte" %}</button>
      </form>
    </div>

  </div>
</div>
{% endblock %}

    “Manage My Account”: two independent forms on the same page.

    • Lines 20–42: the update, using the [MonCompteForm] form: the identity fields, the login, the new password and its confirmation (optional), the current password (required), and the hidden version field;
    • Lines 49–62: Account deletion, a handwritten form with its own field for the current password and a confirmation field. The field has the same name as the one on the first form ([current_password]), but a different ID: two elements on a page cannot have the same ID, as indicated by the attribute [for] for a label. The two forms are independent: the browser sends only the fields from the form whose button was clicked.

    {% extends "layout.html" %}
{% comment %}
  templates/erreur.html - la page d'erreur (400, 403, 404, 405, 419, 500...),
  fabriquée par web/vues/erreurs.py.
{% endcomment %}
{% load i18n %}

{% block contenu %}
<div class="row justify-content-center">
  <div class="col-md-8 col-lg-6">
    <div class="card p-4 text-center">
      <h1 class="display-4 text-danger">{{ code }}</h1>
      <p class="lead">{{ message }}</p>
      <div><a class="btn btn-primary" href="{% url 'accueil' %}">{% translate "Retour à l'accueil" %}</a></div>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
{% endblock %}

    The error page, generated by [web/vues/erreurs.py]: the code HTTP, the message, and a link to the home page ([/], which redirects to the role’s home page or to the login page). It extends the parent template like the other pages: the navigation bar, including the user menu, is also included.

    11.19. Static files

    The [static] folder contains the files that the server sends as-is (example 15): [Bootstrap] ([lib/bootstrap], the stylesheet alone, and its license), a stylesheet, and a script. During development, the [Django] server serves them itself ([django.contrib.staticfiles] application); in production, they are copied to [var/static] by the command [collectstatic], and served by the web server (“A production server”).

    /* =========================================================================
   static/css/styles.css - quelques réglages en plus de Bootstrap
   (les mêmes que dans les autres versions de cette application).
   ========================================================================= */

body {
  background-color: #f5f7fa;
}

.creneau-libre:hover {
  background-color: #e9f7ef;
}

/* -------------------------------------------------------------------------
   .zone-erreur : les messages d'erreur, en bas de page, sur fond rose léger
   (cf. templates/fragments/erreurs.html).
   position: sticky + bottom : si la page est plus haute que la fenêtre (un
   agenda de 12 créneaux, par exemple), la zone reste collée au bas de la
   fenêtre au lieu de disparaître sous la ligne de flottaison - sans jamais
   recouvrir le contenu quand la page est courte.
   z-index : au-dessus du fond grisé de la fenêtre de réservation (.modal-backdrop).
   ------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
.zone-erreur {
  position: sticky;
  bottom: 1rem;
  z-index: 1060;
  margin-top: 1.5rem;
  padding: 0.75rem 1rem;
  background-color: #fdecef; /* light pink */
  border: 1px solid #f5c2c7;
  border-radius: 0.375rem;
  color: #842029;
}

/* the two main options on the patient's "My Account" page */
.carte-option {
  transition: border-color 0.15s, box-shadow 0.15s;
}

.carte-option:hover {
  border-color: #0d6efd;
  box-shadow: 0 0.25rem 0.75rem rgba(13, 110, 253, 0.15);
}

/* the CAPTCHA image (SVG, 150 x 50 pixels) */
.captcha-image svg {
  display: block;
  border: 1px solid #dee2e6;
  border-radius: 0.375rem;
}

    A few additional settings for [Bootstrap], the same as in the other versions of the application.

    • lines 10–12: a bookable slot in the calendar turns green on mouseover;
    • lines 23–33: the error area at the bottom of the page has a light pink background. [position: sticky] with [bottom: 1rem]: if the page is taller than the window (a calendar with 12 time slots), the area remains anchored to the bottom of the window instead of disappearing below the scroll bar; if the page is short, it stays in place without covering anything. [z-index]: It appears over the gray background of the booking window;
    • lines 36–43: the two large “My Account” cards, which light up when the mouse hovers over them;
    • lines 46–50: the CAPTCHA image, with a border.

    // =========================================================================
// static/js/app.js - the application's SEUL JavaScript.
// -------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The entire application works without JavaScript. This script adds a
// convenience feature: before submitting a form that includes the
// data-confirmation="...", a modal window asks "Are you sure?"
// (the window itself is located in the page: templates/fragments/confirmation.html).
// If JavaScript is disabled, the form simply submits without
// confirmation—nothing breaks (the principle of “progressive enhancement”).
//
// Why not window.confirm()? Its input field doesn’t format properly, and its
// buttons remain in the browser’s language, not the page’s.
// =========================================================================

(() => {
  const modale = document.getElementById('modale-confirmation');
  if (!modale) {
    return;
  }
  const message = document.getElementById('modale-confirmation-message');
  const boutonNon = modale.querySelector('.modal-footer [data-action="non"]');

  let formulaireEnAttente = null; // the form to submit if you confirm
  let focusPrecedent = null; // the element to focus on when closing

  function ouvrir(formulaire) {
    formulaireEnAttente = formulaire;
    focusPrecedent = document.activeElement;
     // textContent (not innerHTML): the message is displayed as TEXTE,
     // never interpreted as HTML
    message.textContent = formulaire.dataset.confirmation;
    modale.classList.remove('d-none');
     // the focus moves to "No": accidentally pressing Enter does not delete anything
    boutonNon.focus();
  }

  function fermer() {
    modale.classList.add('d-none');
    formulaireEnAttente = null;
    if (focusPrecedent) {
      focusPrecedent.focus();
    }
  }

   // 1. Form submissions requiring confirmation are intercepted
  document.querySelectorAll('form[data-confirmation]').forEach((formulaire) => {
    formulaire.addEventListener('submit', (evenement) => {
      evenement.preventDefault();
      ouvrir(formulaire);
    });
  });

   // 2. The window’s buttons (Yes / No / close button)
  modale.addEventListener('click', (evenement) => {
    const action = evenement.target.closest('[data-action]')?.dataset.action;
    if (action === 'oui') {
      const formulaire = formulaireEnAttente;
      fermer();
       // formulaire.submit() submits the form SANS to trigger again
       // The 'submit' event: no new confirmation request
      formulaire.submit();
    } else if (action === 'non') {
      fermer();
    } else if (evenement.target.classList.contains('modal')) {
      fermer(); // Click on the grayed-out background, outside the window
    }
  });

   // 3. Keyboard: Esc closes the window; Tab keeps the focus on the window
   /   / (otherwise, the focus would move to the grayed-out page behind it)
  modale.addEventListener('keydown', (evenement) => {
    if (evenement.key === 'Escape') {
      fermer();
    } else if (evenement.key === 'Tab') {
      const boutons = [...modale.querySelectorAll('button')];
      const premier = boutons[0];
      const dernier = boutons[boutons.length - 1];
      if (evenement.shiftKey && document.activeElement === premier) {
        evenement.preventDefault();
        dernier.focus();
      } else if (!evenement.shiftKey && document.activeElement === dernier) {
        evenement.preventDefault();
        premier.focus();
      }
    }
  });
})();

    The only [JavaScript] in the application—the one from Example 21—with a few additions. The entire application works without [JavaScript]: this script adds convenience by providing a confirmation before submitting a form that carries the [data-confirmation] attribute. If [JavaScript] is disabled, the form submits without confirmation: nothing breaks (principle of progressive enhancement).

    • Lines 15–19: The script is a function called as soon as it is defined ([(() => { ... })()]); its variables are not visible to the rest of the page. Without a confirmation window on the page, it does nothing;
    • Lines 26–35: Opening the window: the form to be submitted if the user confirms is stored, and the form’s message is displayed in the window. [textContent], not [innerHTML]: the message is displayed as text and is never interpreted as HTML. Focus moves to the “No” button: accidentally pressing Enter does not delete anything;
    • lines 37–43: closing the window; focus returns to the element that had it previously;
    • lines 46–51: the submission of each form to be confirmed is intercepted ([preventDefault] prevents it), and the window opens. The [submit] event occurs only after the browser’s validations: the current password, which is required ([required]) in the account deletion form, is required before the prompt;
    • lines 54–67: the buttons in the window. A single handler for the entire window: [closest('[data-action]')] finds the clicked button or the element containing it; [?.] ensures [undefined] returns no error if none match. “Yes” submits the form via [formulaire.submit()], which does not trigger the [submit] event: no new confirmation prompt appears. Clicking on the grayed-out background outside the window closes it;
    • lines 71–86: the keyboard. Esc closes the window; the Tab key moves the focus from one button to another without leaving the window (otherwise, it would move to the grayed-out page behind it): this is what users who navigate with the keyboard and screen readers expect.
